title: Complementary restriction of open compact support vanishes at all adic stages
statement: Fix the finite-field datum $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k_0$, and an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $j_0:U_0\hookrightarrow X_0$ be a quasi-compact open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] of separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], and let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be its base change to $k$. Choose a closed immersion $i_0:Z_0\hookrightarrow X_0$ whose image is $X_0\setminus U_0$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], and put $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ after base change to $k$. Fix a finite $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in $\Qlb$, write $R=\mathcal O_E$ with a uniformizer $t$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and take $\Lambda\in\{R,E,\Qlb\}$. Use $Rj_!$ with compactification $(j,\operatorname{id}_X)$ [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] and the completed derived pullback $Li^*$, rationalized and passed to common stages [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. There is a canonical natural isomorphism $z_i:Li^*Rj_!\xrightarrow{\sim}0$ of functors $D^b_c(U,\Lambda)\to D^b_c(Z,\Lambda)$. At the integral stage, after the comparison $d_j$ of [lem-sf-integral-open-reduction-comparison] between $Rj_!$ and termwise localized ringed-site extension by zero, $z_i$ is the completed open base-change comparison of [lem-cbc-completed-extension-zero-comparison] for the cartesian square of $j$ along $i$, whose pulled-back open immersion is $\varnothing\hookrightarrow Z$; its strict finite-reduction maps are the canonical zero restriction maps, not maps chosen from their finite evaluations. At the field stages $z_i$ is the scalar-localized and common-stage image of this integral comparison. It commutes with finite coefficient extension and its associators. In particular, for every algebraically closed field $\Omega$ and every map $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ whose image misses $U$, the complex $Li^*Rj_!L$ pulled back along the induced point of $Z$ is zero, including at geometric points over non-closed points of $X$.

proof.text: Closed immersion composition gives the finite-type and quasi-compact structures on Z₀. The range formula for the actual Over pullback identifies the geometric closed image with the complement of the geometric open image. Scheme.isEmpty_pullback_iff therefore makes the actual square empty. Apply the integral empty-pullback vanishing lemma, which retains the open-reduction and completed base-change route. For each coefficient field this gives zero values of the specified integral functor. Pointwise unique isomorphisms to zero form a natural isomorphism.

The recorded rational pullback object formula and the literal compact-support object formula identify each rational value with localization of the integral value. Localization preserves zero, giving the rational natural zero isomorphism. Its displayed localization equation is uniqueness into zero. The integral zero morphism remains zero under whole-system reduction, since reduction is a left adjoint. Its evaluations remain zero. This is an equality of the strict-system map before any finite evaluation.

The existing open-reduction theorem and integral/completed pullback theorem supply the two comparison witnesses. The empty-cover sheaf axiom makes every module sheaf on the actual empty pullback zero; faithful underlying abelian sheaves reflect this assertion. Homology and the derived t-structure then make every derived object there zero. Exact derived open extension preserves zero. Both ordinary and completed exchanges consequently have zero target and equal zero. The displayed completed comparison equation is uniqueness into the ambient image of the constructible zero object.

For the supplied normalized common-stage compact-support action, its finite_eq and the specified common pullback object formula identify every value with inclusion of its rational value. Stage inclusions preserve zero; hence these values are zero and yield a natural zero isomorphism. The common normalization equation, the specified finite scalar square, and the actual scalar associator equation all have zero target, so uniqueness proves them. The existing scalar morphisms are used with their given sources and targets; no substitute comparisons or arbitrary witnesses are introduced.

For any field-valued point missing U, its image is contained in i(Z). Pullback of i to that field spectrum is a surjective closed immersion onto a reduced scheme, hence an isomorphism. Its inverse followed by the first projection gives the required factorization, without any closedness condition on the image point. The closed complement and the point source are Noetherian of finite dimension. Specialize the existing integral-stratum functoriality theorem with the integral/completed comparison to obtain ambient integral pullback additivity, hence zero preservation and integral vanishing. Rational pullback is additive by its defining specification, so preserves zero. For common pullback, first apply its literal object formula to the inclusion of a zero object at the bottom finite coefficient field; the finite rational pullback and inclusion preserve zero. Functoriality transfers this to the common zero object, so common pullback preserves zero morphisms and zero objects. Apply it to the common vanishing already established.
